recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — name each move in order, and say which general solution formula you would use.

steps.label: Divide by √(a²+b²)
steps.margin_note: First mark, and the step the whole method depends on. Dividing by √(a²+b²) makes the two coefficients a cosine and a sine of the same angle, so the left side becomes ONE trig function.
steps.memory_tip: Divide by √(a² + b²) = 2. That makes both coefficients a sine and a cosine of one angle.

recall.must_convey: That both sides are divided by √(a²+b²) = 2, so the coefficients become √3/2 and 1/2.

steps.why: Divided by √(a²+b²), the coefficients of a sinθ + b cosθ become the cosine and sine of one angle, so one compound-angle formula turns the left side into a single sine.
common_mistakes: Dividing by a + b instead of √(a²+b²).

steps.margin_note: Third mark. sinA cosB − cosA sinB is sin(A−B), so the equation becomes a single sine equal to a single sine. The principal value is then read off directly.
steps.memory_tip: sinA cosB − cosA sinB = sin(A − B), so the angle is θ − π/6 and the principal value is π/4.
